accuracy.evidence: Checked against the topic's evidence (90%+ accuracy on a phonically matched text, rereading for pace and expression, reading with purpose), the English national curriculum Year 1 and Year 2 word-reading statements (read aloud books consistent with developing phonic knowledge; reread to build fluency and confidence; accurately, automatically and without undue hesitation), Common Core RF.K.4 and RF.1.4b (accuracy, appropriate rate and expression on successive readings) and the DfE Reading Framework (fluency is words correct per minute, accuracy matters as well as speed, decodable books match taught GPCs). The 9-in-10 rule is labelled as this topic's 90% level, and the adult text notes many teachers use about 95% for reading alone, so the threshold is not overstated.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented fluency errors: speed as the goal (rocket on the dial, 'Fine if I read fast', 'Leo: the fastest' and the m1 item), word-by-word robot reading (snail, 'The… big… dog…' option, m6), ignoring punctuation and a flat voice (same-words prediction, 'Nothing' and 'Flat' options, m9), books that are too hard (4 and 5 in 10 books, m2), reading once and moving on ('Read it once, then a new one'), and guessing from pictures (adult text and m4).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagfluent is built on the three parts of fluency: phrase scoops drawn under word tiles, a voice card dropped on a line whose end mark is shown large, a finger that glides along one page and stops on still-tricky words with a three-bar read chart, a 10-dot accuracy card per book, and a three-stop speed dial that replays one line. Shingle similarity is 6.7% with flag_sva.js, 6.5% with flag_blend.js and 6.0% with flag_impact.js; Blending (sound buttons and a car) and Sight words (instant recognition) use different mechanisms.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each idea by doing it: wrong breaks get 'breaks up words that go together' with a who/what clue; the same words with . and ? need different voices; the read chart visibly falls from 3 stops to 1 to smooth on the same page; dots make 9 of 10 versus 6 of 10 concrete; and the dial lets them hear snail and rocket fail before picking talking speed, which then draws scoops and a smile.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the next task tests: 'Yes, same words, same voice' (the full-stop and question lines then need Calm and Asking), 'The same: same words' or 'Slower: I am bored of it' for the third read (the chart shows 3, 1, then 0 stops), and 'Just right: I can read most of it' for 4 stuck words in 10 (Space Trip and The Castle go on the too-hard shelf). A.reveal quotes the child's pick in each done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers; why() names the slip: robot ('One word at a time is robot reading'), race ('Fast is not best… you miss the stops'), mark ('? means asking, so your voice goes up'), bang ('A loud, strong voice is for !'), hard ('5 stops in 10 is too many'), once ('Reading it again makes it smoother') and flat ('! asks for a strong voice'). Every wrong tap in the lab also explains itself.

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK 0.5 in very short sentences with concrete examples (the big dog, the cat is asleep). Adult text measures FK 7.4 and uses the precise terms fluency, accuracy, automaticity, rate (words correct per minute), prosody, phrasing, repeated reading and decodable book, with NC Year 1 and 2, Common Core RF.K.4 and RF.1.4b and the DfE Reading Framework.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed; the largest 6-word-shingle overlap with any other lesson is 0.6% (Blending). Kid paragraphs cover scoops, end marks, talking speed and rereading with a just right book; adult paragraphs give the curriculum placement, key terms with the 90% and 95% levels, six named mistakes and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for every step after Show me: word tiles wrap to two or three rows with scoop arcs under each row, the voice cards (78 px tall) and book shelves (70 px) span the width, the read chart labels fit beside the bars, and the speed dial knob is 52 px across with the snail, talking and rocket labels clear. Big button twins below wrap cleanly; desktop was also checked.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five Show me tasks completed, the challenge appeared, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme and there were no console errors. Every canvas action has a button twin (one button per word for scoops, three voice buttons, Read / Sound it out, two shelf buttons, three speed buttons); stuck words on the book card are hollow rings, not colour alone; and the canvas aria-label is updated with every message.
